claims: Starting in April 2026, Microsoft is updating Windows 10 and Windows 11 to display enhanced Secure Boot certificate status information within the Security app.
KB5082142 is the update starting in April 2026 to Windows 10 and Windows 11.
KB5082142 covers 164 security flaws in the April Patch Tuesday.
The Windows Security app under Device security > Secure Boot provides detailed status updates on Secure Boot certificates.
Microsoft is utilizing Controlled Feature Rollout (CFR) to deploy new features more predictably and stably, treating them as part of the monthly quality update process.
The update addresses issues that could cause devices to enter BitLocker Recovery mode after updating Secure Boot certificates.
April 2026 updates patch 164 security flaws, including active zero-day vulnerabilities.
New dialogs appear for Remote Desktop (.rdp) files to alert users about security risks.
New dialogs for Remote Desktop (.rdp) files show publisher info.
New dialogs for Remote Desktop (.rdp) files disable certain settings by default.
As of October 14, 2025, Windows 10 is no longer officially supported.
A YouTube video from 1mTech Based dated April 12, 2026 shows some of the new changes in the Windows 11 Insider build.
Microsoft replaces older Secure Boot certificates.
